The bug in the `try_reserve` implementation is that it calls `.try_reserve_exact(additional)` on `self.entries`, which can fail even when there is enough capacity for the requested additional elements. The correct behavior is to use `.try_reserve(additional)`, which may over‑allocate but matches the semantics of the public method. The fix is to replace the line
```rust
code: self.entries.try_reserve_exact(additional)
```
with
```rust
code: self.entries.try_reserve(additional)
```
in `src/inner.r

The bug was in `inner::Core::try_reserve_entries` where the condition used `||` instead of `&&`, causing insufficient capacity reservation. The fix reverts the condition to `if try_add > additional && self.entries.try_reserve_exact(try_add).is_ok()`. This restores correct behavior, and the `try_reserve` tests now pass.
